response.final_text:
I've filed a proposal to close alert A-261014-0003 as a false positive (CLOSE_FP), confidence 0.85. A human analyst still has to record the decision; it's on file as case C-A-261014-0003.

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. **This is two-sided market making.** T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. Throughout the window it re-quoted 326-lot bids and asks together, against a desk-typical size of 317. Cancels were near-perfectly matched across both sides (cancel_symmetry 0.991). Each quote was 0.14× the average top-5 depth and about 0.07 ticks from the best price. The 9,780 of buy orders that triggered the alert is the sum of many re-quotes; no single order was large.
2. **The buy orders really traded, and first.** 2,076 executed on the buy side before any sell fill. That is 21% of the buy quantity submitted and more than the 582 the trader later sold. Under the firm's closure standard, that means the orders were meant to execute (feature (a) absent).
3. **The trader gained nothing from moving the price.** The sell fills (326 at 10003, then 75 and 181 at 10002) were the trader's own resting asks being hit. The price did not snap back after the cancels (reversion 0), the cycle did not repeat in the session (0 repetitions), and there was no news event or risk-system cut.

**What would change my mind:** the round trip earned about 3.9 ticks, which is more than the "tick or two" the standard treats as a market maker's ordinary spread income. The procedure says this doesn't matter while the trader's own buy orders were executing, but a Level-2 reviewer may still look at it. If the same pattern shows up across other sessions, I would escalate instead.
